summary: The exact candidate is a substantive partial fix. It fixes the current paged-attention factory's stale wrapper after an ordinary helper rebind and fixes the prior review's shared-code closure, __defaults__, and __kwdefaults__ counterexamples. It still reuses stale wrappers when relevant state changes inside a custom object used as a helper default or inside a callable helper instance.

gpu_execution.evidence: One assigned AMD Instinct MI350X (gfx950) ran the recorded CPU-referenced numerical sanity check. The cache regression itself is architecture-independent and was measured by wrapper identity and captured values.

remaining_counterexamples: A statically referenced helper whose default is a mutable custom object remains stale when an attribute of that default object changes: the same wrapper is returned and retains the old captured result.

A statically referenced callable helper instance remains stale when state used by its __call__ method changes: __call__ is not traversed and the callable snapshot contains only stable identity/no code.
remaining_limitations: The candidate is Python-only, so native rebuilding was not applicable. Python loaded from /job/repo/python and native code from /job/repo/python/flydsl/_mlir/_mlir_libs/_mlir.cpython-312-x86_64-linux-gnu.so. The issue-era compile_pa_decode_ps function and supplied end-to-end script are absent at the recorded base; the current compile_pa_decode_tile factory was used for repository-level failing-before/passing-after wrapper evidence. No end-to-end PA numerical launch was claimed. Automatic dependency discovery also documents/retains limitations around dynamic getattr and descriptor-hidden state.
